challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to .faff/ at all, not only committing them; gitignore addresses only the repo half. Caching literal API keys in .faff/cache/credentials.json puts plaintext secrets on disk where logs, backups, run artifacts, cage mounts and evidence bundles can pick them up. The claimed benefit is weak: reading process.env is an in-memory lookup, and an in-process variable would remove any re-read cost without touching disk. The why does not show that the old rationale stopped holding; it trades a security invariant for a negligible latency gain.
